title: observability-driven reingestion with sample-fidelity checks and cost-aware throttling
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: We need a safer, cheaper way to reingest historical usage records for the Console backend when metrics are invalidated by bugs or schema changes. Current bulk backfills either run at full blast (expensive, DB-throttled) or rely on ad-hoc scripts with poor visibility.

Goal: Build an orchestrator that performs controlled reingestion of historical console events with: sample-based fidelity validation (compare a small, representative subset of reprocessed outputs to golden metrics), schema-aware transformations during ingest, lineage-preserving idempotency tokens, and a cost-aware throttling controller that adapts concurrency to DB/compute pressure and budget constraints.

Scope: This ticket covers the orchestrator MVP (controller + worker integration hooks), sample validator, basic telemetry dashboards, and a pilot run for the last 90 days of Console route metrics for 2 customers. Full rollout to all tenants will be a follow-up after validation and runbook signoff.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can launch a target reingest job over a specified time window and persist job metadata with per-chunk checkpoints
Workers apply schema migration transforms automatically when an event version mismatch is detected
Sample validator picks stratified samples and produces a fidelity report with delta against golden metrics (token counts, latency percentiles, error rates)
Cost-aware throttler reduces worker concurrency when DB throttling or cloud spend threshold is breached and resumes when safe
Jobs are idempotent: rerunning the same chunks does not double-insert events and preserves upstream event lineage tags
steps: Design controller API and job metadata model (job -> chunk -> checkpoint -> lineageID)
Implement worker hooks for schema-aware transform and idempotent upsert path
Add sample selector component (time stratified + route/tenant weighting)
Implement sample validator that computes side-by-side metrics and produces a human-readable report
Add a throttler that monitors DB error rates, CPU, and a soft cost budget signal to modulate concurrency
Wire up observability dashboards and run a 90-day pilot for two tenants
Create runbook and rollback steps for operational runs
decisions: Use per-chunk SHA256 lineage tokens rather than global sequence numbers to keep jobs resumable across schema changes
Perform schema transforms in the worker to avoid a separate pre-processing pipeline (simpler rollback and visibility)
Sampling strategy chosen: stratified by tenant + route, 1% overall sample with minimum 100 events per route
Throttler will expose both 'cost budget' and 'safety budget' signals — cost budget set by PM; safety budget derived from DB 429 rate and tail latency
blockers: Need final sign-off from Data Privacy on persistent lineage tokens (PRD link in links)
Access to expanded test harness that can simulate DB 429 for throttler tuning (infra ticket outstanding)
Feature flags for enabling reingest on a per-tenant basis not yet available in Console admin
